feed.title: The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour

items.title: Japanese firms warming up to Bangladesh
items.snippet: Japanese companies are increasingly looking to Bangladesh, attracted by its large consumer base, growing middle class and potential for investment.

items.title: Country’s only DAP fertiliser plant remains shut for 4 months
items.snippet: The country’s only diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertiliser factory has been shut for nearly four months due to a shortage of phosphoric acid -- a key raw material -- with a government approval delay holding up fresh imports.

items.title: ADP spending hits 17-year low in Q1
items.snippet: The government’s development spending in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27) fell to its lowest level in at least 17 years, raising concerns about its ability to implement budget plans and support economic growth.

items.title: Websites still vulnerable despite cyber warnings
items.snippet: Several government and private organisations in Bangladesh are using outdated or unsupported versions of PHP, a programming language widely used to build websites, potentially leaving their public-facing online services vulnerable to cyberattacks, the government’s cyber security agency has warned.

items.title: BB to relax lending rules for Tk 1,700cr City Group bailout
items.snippet: Eight private commercial banks are set to receive regulatory relief to extend Tk 1,700 crore in fresh loans to debt-laden City Group, in a move aimed at keeping its operations running and ensuring supplies of essential commodities ahead of Ramadan.

items.title: What happens after LDC graduation?
items.snippet: Bangladesh is seeking to defer its LDC graduation even as it prepares for the transition, amid concerns over export competitiveness and preferential market access. How have the eight countries that graduated before it fared, and what lessons do their experiences hold for Bangladesh?

items.title: Sri Lanka seeks faster green energy shift after oil shocks
items.snippet: Sri Lanka is determined to accelerate its transition to renewable energy spurred by soaring oil prices, but faces major constraints, its energy minister told AFP.

items.title: Pharma exports need stronger logistics to compete globally
items.snippet: The United States’ decision to apply a zero additional tariff rate to specified specialty pharmaceutical products and associated ingredients from Bangladesh presents a significant opportunity.

items.title: UK consumer confidence tumbles
items.snippet: British consumer confidence has suffered its sharpest month-on-month fall since early in the Covid-19 pandemic as economic worries deepen, according ​to a survey that created an unwelcome backdrop for finance ‌minister John Healey’s budget next week.

items.title: Afghan trade halt hits Pakistan’s pharma exports
items.snippet: After contracting by 30.26 percent in FY26, Pakistan’s pharmaceutical exports continued to decline, falling 25.53 percent in value in the first quarter of 2026-27.
